awd_abstract_narration:
This award will provide funding for the “Integers Conference 2025,” which will be held in Athens, Georgia, May 14-17, 2025. The conference is being hosted by the Department of Mathematics of the University of Georgia. The Integers conferences, of which this will be the tenth, serve to bring together mathematicians and students interested in the fields of combinatorics and number theory. The conference will promote interaction among research mathematicians at all career stages ranging from undergraduate mathematics students to internationally distinguished researchers. A significant portion of the funding will support students and early-career faculty.

The conference will serve as a catalyst for major collaborative projects among mathematicians representing the areas of additive number theory, multiplicative number theory, combinatorial game theory, probabilistic number theory, enumerative combinatorics, combinatorial optimization, Ramsey theory, the theory of partitions, and other areas of number theory and combinatorics. It will feature twelve plenary speakers and about fifty additional speakers. The conference organizers intend to include a number of student research talks, including talks presented by students who have recently participated in NSF “Research Experiences for Undergraduates” programs. The proceedings of the conference will be published as a special volume of the journal Integers. The following website has been created for the conference: https://sites.google.com/view/integersconference2025

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The Integers Conference 2025 was held May 14 - May 17, 2025 at the University ofGeorgia in Athens, Georgia. The conference had seventeen plenary talks as well sixty-seven 20-minute contributed talks. The plenary speakers were Florian Luca,, Jean-Marc Deshouillers, Carrie Finch-Smith, Alex Iosevich, Jeffrey Lagarias, Melvyn Nathanson, David Ross, Kevin O’Bryant, Nathan McNew, Paul Pollack, Catherine Turnage-Butterbaugh, Steve Fan, Jared Duker Lichtman, Lola Thompson, Andrew Granville, Katherine Stange, and David and Gregory Chudnovsky.  The talks represented recent research advances in a variety of areas of number theory and combinatorics, including additive number theory, multiplicative number theory, the theory of partitions, elementary number theory, sequences, polynomials, combinatorial game theory, Ramsey theory, and enumerateive combinatorics.  One of themain goals of the conference was to recruit both graduate and undergraduate students, and to allow them to mingle with, and learn from, more expeirenced researchers in number theory and combinatorics. As it turned out, twenty-three of the speakers were students, including seven undergraduate students. There were also numerous presentations given by early-careermathematics. With the goal of successfully disseminating the ideas and results generated by the conference, all speakers were invited to submit articles for a special volume of the research journal Integers,which will consist of the Proceedings of the conference. Twenty-five articles have been accepted for the Proceedings,, which we anticipate being published in August, 2026.  We are also aiming to have the Proceedings published in the form of a book, entitled "Combinatorics and Number Theory; Proceedings of the Integers Conference 2025."
